title: calendula suffruticosa subsp. algarbiensis
intro: Calendula suffruticosa subsp. algarbiensis, commonly known as Spanish Marigold, is a subspecies of the Calendula genus, characterized by its compact growth habit and smaller flowers compared to other Calendula species. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including wound healing, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Calendula suffruticosa subsp. algarbiensis include tissue repair, immune system modulation, and protection against oxidative stress, attributed to its bioactive constituents such as flavonoids, terpenoids, and carotenoids. The bioactive constituents of Calendula suffruticosa subsp. algarbiensis, including triterpenoid saponins, have been shown to contribute to its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial activities.
